story.A: Sam Lee signs up two companies by text. Then Alex books an 11:00am drop-off at Lee's Instrument Shop, Sat Oct 24, for a guitar that buzzes on the low strings. Mina inspects it and writes an estimate. Once Alex OKs it, Mina does the work and texts READY when it's done. Pick a money choice at the top to follow its path.
story.B: Sam Lee signs up two companies by text. Then Alex books Lee Music Service to tune a piano at home, at 9 Linden Way, and Owen comes Thu Oct 22 between 8 and 10am. The job depends on the money choice you pick: the piano tuning, a piano priced at the visit, or a school band room repair priced from photos.

notes:
From repair-shop (from: repair-shop), refitted Tue Oct 27 and merged on the REDESIGN 2 master (frozen 9:17am). A musical instrument shop runs like a device repair shop: the instrument is dropped off, an inspection is OK'd, a written estimate is OK'd before any work, and READY comes before the pick-up. No base plug-in or old flowchart existed (new profession); the plug-in is built from the trade's norm.
Two companies: Lee's Instrument Shop (the master's barbershop, flow A: the shop for guitars, violins, woodwinds and brass) and Lee Music Service (the master's Lee Home Services, flow B: a repair tech who tunes pianos at homes and studios and repairs band instruments at schools). Kinds of work: plumbing became band instrument repair, electrical became piano tuning, the later NEW kind is school band visits (B) and bow rehair (A). People: Riley and Avery became Mina and Theo (the shop); Jordan and Casey became Owen and Lena (on-site), so the master's pronouns still fit (Jordan he, Casey she). Addresses: 52 Harbor St (the shop), 9 Linden Way (Alex), 88 Willow Rd (the second site).
No license: instrument repair needs no person license; the business gives its registration where the city or state asks (S1-60 '1 A license', S2-28 '1 Yes, each one' and S11-42's two license branches are off; the sign-up license sentences are reworded as registration only). A secondhand dealer license matters only if the shop buys used instruments (pf.rules.secondhand, a switch); Rosie books repair services only.
Flow A money: main visit|none|counter (a guitar that buzzes on the low strings: the $25 inspection is promised, Mina's written estimate is $110 fret level + $15 new strings = $125 with the inspection included), list|none|counter ($35 restring), visit|none|bill (the bill goes with READY), list|deposit|counter ($140 woodwind overhaul, a long repair: $40 deposit books the bench, $100 at the counter). The shop saves no card and takes no full price: no cancel or no-show fee at the shop.
Flow B money: main list|card|bill ($179 piano tuning at the customer's place; a card is saved for the $89 trip fee, which is the late-cancel and no-show fee, charged only on Sam's yes, and owed after a no to a visit price: B4-14), visit|card|bill (a piano with sticking keys, priced at the visit), list|card|card (the saved card charged at DONE), photos|deposit|bill (a school band room repair priced from photos and the list of instruments: $640, $160 deposit, $480 on the bill). No full price anywhere. All amounts have names per path.
Facts: dropoff, photos (a crack or a band room priced from photos), extrawork (a part found at the bench, OK'd first). No documents fact: the written estimate is the visit path's own price OK (A8-29 / B8-93), so B8-93's 'An estimate becomes its own job' branch is off. No switches. Settings: A a set start (drop-off slots), B a 2-hour window; cutoff 24 hours before.
Safety: fire, smoke, an injury or a piano that fell stops the booking; a piano that could tip, a strong smell of glue or lacquer, or a snapped string gets the safety steps, then the booking goes on, marked urgent. A cracked pinblock found during tuning stops the work (B8-30). A child is never the person served: a parent books for a student's instrument (A4-24 / B4-32 'A child' off).
Own step: A8-x01, the condition log at the counter (make and model, photos of the instrument and case, the serial number and stated value on the secure page), a real first step of this trade.
Offs for work this shop never has: video or phone (A4-01, B4-01), plans and insurance, packages, a person by name, plan steps, rented items, 'too few booked', a child left, stage billing, next visit at checkout, a signed contract, nobody-home branches and sent-now steps.
Not sure (for the verifier): S1-13's sign-up example card still lists 'Paid in full' lines and a $20 fee for services this shop never prepays (master text); A8-02 keeps the 'something required is missing' branch for a violin with no bow; a school (an organization) books and pays through the master's organization branch (A4-89, B4-107), with no overlay words; the free piano condition check in the master's amounts is used by no listed path.
